title: In‑Memory Authentication
description: Configure users and roles directly in Java code.

slides.title: UserDetailsService & In‑Memory Users 👥
slides.content:
# Define Users in Code

You can create a `SecurityFilterChain` bean that configures authentication and authorization. For in‑memory users, we use `InMemoryUserDetailsManager`.

quizData.question: Which class is used to manage in‑memory users in Spring Security?
quizData.explanation: InMemoryUserDetailsManager is an implementation of UserDetailsService that stores user details in memory.

slides.title: Configuring In‑Memory Users
Password Encoding 🗝️
Role Prefix
slides.content: Spring Security automatically adds `ROLE_` prefix to roles. So `roles("USER")` becomes `ROLE_USER` internally. You'll see this when using expressions like `hasRole('USER')`.
